criteria.text: The memo identifies that the Saltmarsh Pavilion venue license with Kestrel Bay Parks Conservancy requires the Conservancy's consent to a change of control of Lumenhall, yet the SPA's no-third-party-consent representation (Section 4.5) and Buyer's closing condition (Section 7.2(d)) cover only the Required Consents and do not include this consent. It explains that Buyer could be obliged to close without the consent and risk termination of the license, with only a capped representation claim as remedy, and it recommends adding the consent as a Required Consent or closing condition, or obtaining a specific uncapped indemnity.

The memo identifies that Paragraph 3 of the Side Letter subjects Losses from breach of SPA Section 4.12 (Taxes) to the Indemnity Cap. This removes the tax carve-out in SPA Section 8.4(b). The memo explains that the Side Letter controls over the SPA under the order-of-precedence clause (Section 10.3), so pre-Closing tax losses become capped, and it recommends amending the Side Letter to restore the tax exclusion.

The memo identifies that the Escrow Agreement (Section 12.6, and/or Section 5.3 on release on a final order) selects Delaware law and the exclusive Delaware Court of Chancery forum, which conflicts with the SPA's New York law and New York County forum. It explains that Buyer could be forced into separate Delaware litigation to reach the escrow even after winning in New York, and it recommends conforming the Escrow Agreement to New York law and forum or having it accept a final New York order.

The memo identifies that the Escrow Agreement's definition of 'Indemnifiable Claim' (Section 1.1, used in Section 4.2) covers only representation and warranty claims under SPA Section 8.2(a). It explains that covenant-breach and Pre-Closing Tax claims therefore cannot be paid from the escrow, even though SPA Section 2.4(a) says the escrow secures all Indemnifiable Losses, and it recommends conforming the definition to cover all of Section 8.2.
The memo states that the SPA's Indemnity Cap is 10% of the Purchase Price, or equivalently $8,640,000.
The memo states that under the SPA's order of precedence the Side Letter prevails over the Stock Purchase Agreement.
The memo is structured as a list of discrete issues. For each issue it gives the document and section reference, explains why the issue matters to the client, and gives a recommended fix.
The memo presents the issues in an order of importance to the client, or explicitly ranks or prioritises them.

The memo does not conclude that pre-Closing tax losses remain uncapped or excluded from the Indemnity Cap under the deal documents as executed, for example by relying solely on SPA Section 8.4(b) without accounting for the Side Letter.
The memo does not conclude that the Conservancy's change-of-control consent for the venue license has been obtained or is already a Required Consent or closing condition under the executed SPA.
